fact: One of the two Pointer stars that guide the eye from the Dipper to the Pole Star.
bio: Dubhe (Alpha Ursae Majoris) is an orange giant about 123 light-years away, one of the two 'Pointers' at the front of the bowl of the Big Dipper. A line drawn through Dubhe and its neighbour Merak points almost exactly at Polaris.
cultural: The name is Arabic for 'the bear'. The Pointers have guided travellers to the North Star for millennia, making Dubhe one of the most practically useful stars in the northern sky.
